title: Halcyon Fintech privacy constraints jot
body:
Meeting: Halcyon Financial Services — internal notes (post-call)
Date: 2024-09-11 (call with Halcyon infra + legal)
Attendees: Asha (RWI), Liam (RWI), Sofia (RWI), Mark Patel (Halcyon CTO), Priya Rao (Halcyon Head of Compliance), Dan Lee (Halcyon SRE)
Purpose: quick scoping conversation: privacy constraints, networking model (air-gapped vs VPC), KMS expectations, audit log retention, latency SLAs for fraud-score API

High-level summary
- Halcyon is evaluating Redwood Private for a pilot: 2 GPU nodes colocated in AWS GovCloud region, potential air-gap on-prem for production later.
- Primary constraints: strict PII handling, auditability (immutable logs for 7 years), customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys, and a requirement for no external model telemetry leaving their VPC.
- Functional target: run a fraud-score LM endpoint that processes short transaction contexts (avg 120 tokens) with 100 RPS burst, 99th percentile latency target ~150ms for inference.

Technical notes / requirements captured
- Data residency and egress
  - All payloads must remain within customer VPC/GovCloud. No model telemetry or usage telemetry may be sent to Redwood hosted control plane without explicit opt-in.
  - Control plane must support a private endpoint or customer-run control plane. Halcyon prefers customer-managed control plane for compliance.

- KMS / key management
  - Must integrate with customer AWS KMS with HSM (no Redwood-managed keys in pilot).
  - Keys used for model encryption and token store encryption. Flow: Redwood Private instance must call customer KMS only over VPC endpoints.
  - Bring-your-own-key rotation policy: Halcyon wants monthly rotation with zero-downtime rewrap. Need to confirm support for key-rotation workflows.

- Logging & audit
  - Immutable request/response audit log requirement for 7 years. Logs cannot contain full prompt text for PII reasons; Halcyon needs redaction pipeline or token-based references (hashes) + separate secure vault with raw capture under strict access controls.
  - All logs must be exportable to customer S3 with server-side encryption and MFA delete enabled.

- Network & deployment topology
  - Pilot: 2x p4d-like GPUs in GovCloud (single AZ), private control plane inside Halcyon VPC.
  - Future: on-prem sealed box option (air-gapped) – need OEM docs and install checklist.
  - Egress rules: strict deny to internet except customer-maintained endpoints.

- Performance & inference details
  - Model family: open Llama-3-variant or similar; Halcyon will test both FP16 and 4-bit quantized builds.
  - Throughput/latency: PoC target 100rps sustained at 120 tokens avg, 99p latency <=150ms. If not achievable on single-node we'll evaluate batching/replicas.
  - KV cache persistence: they want warm cache across restarts where possible. Confirm persistence options and storage encryption.

- Security/compliance
  - SOC2 + ISO27001 required for Redwood Private package. Halcyon asked for SOC2 report and penetration test summary.
  - Option: Redwood signs Data Processing Addendum (DPA) with addendum for financial data. Priya requested a draft DPA/BAA variant.

Gotchas / open questions (capture and follow-up items)
- Can Redwood Private run fully offline (air-gapped) workflows for model updates? What is the process for pushing model updates without Internet?
- Does Redwood support KMS HSM-backed rotation with rewrap zero-downtime? If not, outline suggested migration steps.
- Audit logs: need a design proposal showing how to store hashes vs redacted content and how to allow forensic access under controls.
- Latency target is aggressive for 120-token avg at 100rps on p4d-equivalent; need performance test plan. Potential mitigation: model distillation or smaller variant as fallback.
- Telemetry: Halcyon forbids any usage stats leaving the VPC by default. Need to enumerate what control-plane telemetry Redwood expects and provide an opt-in toggle.
- Can we support export of logs to customer S3 that uses SSE-KMS with their key and MFA delete? Verify compatibility.

Immediate next steps / action items
- Asha: draft initial PoC statement of work (SoW) with scope: GovCloud pilot, control plane model, KMS integration, performance testing plan. Due: 2024-09-18. (JIRA-5821)
- Liam: validate key-rotation support and write short tech note on rewrap behavior with AWS KMS; propose workaround if live rewrap is unsupported. Due: 2024-09-16.
- Sofia: assemble compliance artifacts (SOC2 summary, pen test recs) and produce internal red team checklist for air-gapped install. Due: 2024-09-20.
- Mark (Halcyon): provide their S3 bucket policy template and sample KMS key ARN. Due: 2024-09-15.

Call slack follow-ups
- Post a short recap to #halcyon-onboard and request Halcyon to confirm: (1) whether control plane must be customer-run for pilot, (2) whether they can accept hashed prompts in logs vs full text.

Notes to self / heuristics for the PoC
- Keep telemetry opt-out-first. Design privacy-first defaults for Private installs.
- Build the SoW modularly: separate networking, data, keys, logging, and perf. Halcyon will want direct line items for cost estimation per module.
- Prep a small perf runbook with knobs: model variant, quantization, batch size, KV cache warm strategy, async fallback to smaller model for high tail latency.

Rough risk assessment
- High risk: inability to meet latency SLA on chosen hardware leading to architectural rework.
- Medium risk: KMS rotation constraints and log redaction complexity.
- Low risk: SOC2 docs — available but might require clarifications.

References / quick links
- Internal: /confluence/infra/private-deployments-install-guide (ask infra-eng for updated steps)
- Ticket: JIRA-5821 (PoC SoW)

End of jot.
(Informal — keep in users/ for now, will move to shared_drives/company if SoW finalized)
